readme: goodenizer-demo — the dynamics and dirt processors, one of each, wired up.
Five processors ship for making things sound good rather than making them
sound different. Four do one job each; the fifth is all four in a box:
compressor   evens out level        (here: 'squash', on the smash bus)
saturator    adds harmonics/dirt    (here: 'grit', on keys)
tilt         trades lows for highs  (here: 'voice', on keys)
limiter      holds a ceiling        (here: 'cap', on the smash bus)
goodenizer   all four in order      (here: 'glue', on master)
Everything is stopped-clock repeatable — the euclidean grid plays the same
bar every pass — so you can A/B any of these and actually hear the change
rather than a different take.
Start with the master chain:
/start
/glue                      live gain reduction, both stages
/glue mix=0                the session with nothing on it
/glue mix=1 2              fade it back in over 2 seconds
/glue tone=-0.6 4b         tilt it dark; +0.6 for thin and bright
/glue threshold=-45 ratio=18   full squash
It ships with drive=1, which means its saturation stage is present but
clean. Compression, tilt and limiting make a mix more like itself —
louder, steadier, better balanced. Saturation makes it into something
else, so it waits to be asked:
/glue drive=9              stop being polite
/glue character=fold       a wavefolder. soft | hard | fold | tape
/glue drive=1              back to clean
'glue' is a composite: /glue threshold= and /squash threshold= are the
same control on two different compressors, not two implementations.
Parallel compression — the smash bus is a squashed copy of the drums,
blended back underneath them rather than replacing them:
/smash gain=0             drums, untreated
/smash gain=0.9 4b        bring the squashed copy up under them
/squash                   watch it reduce 15dB+
/squash mix=0.4           or do the blend inside the compressor instead
/cap ceiling=-14          the limiter after it, clamping harder
Dirt and tone on the keys, two processors in series on one track:
/grit drive=20            tape saturation, pushed
/grit character=hard      buzzy odd harmonics, no rounding
/grit mix=0.5             parallel distortion
/voice tone=0.8 4b        pull the keys forward and thin
/voice pivot=2500         move where the see-saw pivots
The pumping compressor. 'sidechain' is an LFO patched into glue.threshold,
so the threshold itself moves in time and the whole mix breathes with it:
/patches                  find its id
/patch id=<id> depth=18   from a breath to a full four-to-the-floor pump
/sidechain freq=1.8       half-time pumping at this tempo
Any param above ramps (tone=0.8 4b) and defers (drive=9 at=cycle) like
every other param in the engine — including threshold, which is what makes
the sidechain patch work at all.
